components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default action for progressing or saving an administrator decision.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 36px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--brand-dark, #557129); color: #fff; font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #4a6422; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand, #7ea243) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A bordered action for alternate or lower-emphasis workflow steps.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 36px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 14px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #dfe3dd); border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; color: var(--foreground, #262a25); font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--muted, #f1f2ef); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand, #7ea243) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: A quiet utility action that gains a surface only on interaction.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { min-height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground, #687067); font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: color 150ms, background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--muted, #f1f2ef); color: var(--foreground, #262a25); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand, #7ea243) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: A clearly labeled irreversible or destructive administrator action.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { min-height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--danger, #c4473a); color: #fff; font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: var(--danger-dark, #8d2d24); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--danger, #c4473a) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The standard compact field for settings and operational entry.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: var(--foreground, #262a25); font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field { width: 100%; height: 36px; box-sizing: border-box; border: 1px solid var(--border, #dfe3dd); border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; padding: 0 10px; color: var(--foreground, #262a25); font: 400 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--brand, #7ea243); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand, #7ea243) 30%, transparent); }

components.name: Success Badge
components.description: A compact status label for positive or completed states.
components.css: .ds-badge-success { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand, #7ea243) 30%, transparent); border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--brand-soft, #eff5e7); color: var(--brand-dark, #557129); font: 500 12px/16px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Primary Navigation Item
components.description: A left-rail destination with a quiet default and tinted active state.
components.html: Sub Plan›
components.css: .ds-nav-item { height: 36px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 16px 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--brand-soft, #eff5e7); color: var(--brand-dark, #557129); text-decoration: none; font: 500 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--muted, #f1f2ef); color: var(--foreground, #262a25); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand, #7ea243) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Operational Metric Card
components.description: A compact count and label used in the daily planning summary.
components.css: .ds-metric-card { min-width: 150px; display: grid; gap: 4px; padding: 12px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #dfe3dd); border-radius: 8px; background: #fff; color: var(--foreground, #262a25); font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-metric-card span { color: var(--muted-foreground, #687067); font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; } .ds-metric-card strong { font-size: 20px; line-height: 28px; }

narrative.overview: The interface should feel like a well-kept administrator's desk at the start of a busy school day: calm enough to reduce pressure, compact enough to keep related facts in view, and utilitarian enough that every control earns its place. Warm neutral surfaces keep the workspace approachable, while green accents connect actions and active states to the product identity without turning the screen into decoration. The system favors trustworthy structure over spectacle. Thin borders, steady alignment, short labels, and predictable controls let administrators scan quickly and act with confidence. Its incumbent character is calm, compact, utilitarian, warm, and trustworthy. The descriptive palette names capture the current implementation; they are not permanent brand constraints. During an overhaul, semantic roles and contrast treatments may evolve when evidence supports a clearer or more accessible system.
keyCharacteristics: Compact laptop-first workspaces with clear operational hierarchy.
Warm gray-green neutrals and one restrained accent family.
Flat, border-led surfaces with shadow reserved for overlays.
Direct controls, short labels, and visible state language.
Accessible contrast and status cues that never depend on color alone.

rules.name: The Evolving Token Rule
rules.body: Apple Green, Deep Moss, Pale Leaf, and Warm Paper are descriptive names for the incumbent tokens. Preserve their current meaning when extending this system, but allow an explicitly approved overhaul to improve semantic roles or contrast.

rules.name: The Contrast-Safe Action Rule
rules.body: Use the darker green treatment for filled controls with small white text. Raw Apple Green remains an accent unless the foreground treatment passes the required contrast.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Amber communicates warning and red communicates danger. Never reuse those colors as decorative categories.

rules.name: The Operational Scale Rule
rules.body: Keep the hierarchy compressed: 24px is the normal page-title ceiling, and most working content stays between 12px and 16px.

rules.name: The Weight-Before-Size Rule
rules.body: Prefer weight and spacing to large jumps in type size when raising emphasis inside dense workspaces.

rules.name: The Work-in-View Rule
rules.body: Prefer arrangements that keep dates, status, filters, and the current decision area visible together on a laptop screen.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface at rest uses a border and tonal contrast, not a shadow. Add depth only when the interaction introduces a real layer.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Use 6px for controls, 8px for containers, 12px only for unusually prominent compositions, and a full pill only for compact status or filter labels.

rules.name: The Decision Clarity Rule
rules.body: Every state-changing control must pair its visual treatment with explicit action text, status text, or an icon with an accessible label.

dos: **Do** keep the current task, date, status, and next action visible together when space allows.
**Do** use borders and quiet tonal fills to organize resting surfaces.
**Do** use the Apple Green family sparingly for identity, selection, and action emphasis.
**Do** use Deep Moss for small white-on-green controls when contrast requires the darker treatment.
**Do** pair status color with text or an icon and preserve visible keyboard focus.
**Do** keep routine controls near the 36px height and the 12–14px type range.
donts: **Don't** treat the descriptive token names as permanent constraints during an explicitly approved overhaul.
**Don't** use raw Apple Green behind small white text without verifying contrast.
**Don't** use brand green as a schedule category color.
**Don't** add shadows to ordinary cards, tables, or navigation rows.
**Don't** inflate the hierarchy with oversized display type or spacious marketing-page rhythms.
**Don't** communicate warning, danger, Assigned, or Unresolved states through color alone.
